name: float
description: floats a window

name: tile
description: tiles a window

name: fullscreen
description: fullscreens a window

name: maximize
description: maximizes a window

name: persistentsize
description: allows size persistence between application launches for floating windows

name: fullscreenstate
description: sets the focused window’s fullscreen mode and the one sent to the client
help:
fullscreenstate [internal] [client] sets the fullscreen state of a window. internal controls how Hyprland treats the window (e.g., maximize or fullscreen), and client tells the app what state it thinks it's in.
Values: 0 = none, 1 = maximize, 2 = fullscreen, 3 = maximize + fullscreen.
Example: fullscreenstate 1 2 means Hyprland maximizes the window internally, while the app believes it's in fullscreen mode — useful for apps that behave differently when "fullscreened."

name: move
description: moves a floating window
help:
move [x] [y] positions a floating window using integers or percentages.
You can use values like 20, 50%, or anchors like 100%-20 to align from the right/bottom.
Special forms:

    100%-w-20 → subtracts the window's width/height for precise edge gaps

    cursor [x] [y] → positions window relative to cursor

    onscreen → ensures the window stays within screen bounds

Example: move 100%-w-10 100%-h-10 puts the window in the bottom-right with a 10px gap.

name: size
description: resizes a floating window
help:
size [x] [y] resizes a floating window using integers or percentages.
You can prefix values with:

    < → set a maximum size (e.g. <500, <80%)

    > → set a minimum size (e.g. >200, >20%)

    No prefix → set exact size (e.g. 600 400 or 50% 70%)

Examples:

    size 800 600 → sets size to 800×600 pixels

    size <90% <90% → limits max size to 90% of screen

    size >300 >300 → ensures minimum size of 300×300 pixels

name: center
description: centers the floating window on the monitor
help:
center [opt] centers a floating window on its monitor.

    If opt is 1, it respects monitor-reserved areas (like top bars or docks).

    If omitted or 0, it centers the window regardless of reserved space.

Examples:

    center → center the window normally

    center 1 → center the window but avoid reserved areas (e.g., bar at the top)

name: pseudo
description: pseudotiles a window

name: monitor
description: sets the monitor on which a window should open
help:
monitor [id] sets the monitor where a window should open.
You can use either the numeric ID (e.g. 1, 0) or the monitor name (e.g. DP-1, HDMI-A-1).

Examples:

    monitor 1 → open the window on monitor ID 1

    monitor DP-1 → open the window on the monitor named DP-1

name: workspace
description: sets the workspace on which a window should open
help:
workspace [w] sets the workspace where a window should open.

    [w] can be a number (e.g. 1) or a special name (e.g. special:music)

    Use unset to remove previous workspace rules for this window

    Add silent after the workspace to open the window without switching focus to it

Examples:

    workspace 2 → opens the window on workspace 2

    workspace special:chat → sends the window to the "chat" special workspace

    workspace unset → clears any previously assigned workspace

    workspace 1 silent → opens on workspace 1 without focusing it

name: noinitialfocus
description: disables the initial focus to the window

name: pin
description: pins the window (i.e. show it on all workspaces)

name: unset
description: removes all previously set rules for the given parameters

name: nomaxsize
description: removes max size limitations

name: stayfocused
description: forces focus on the window as long as it’s visible

name: group
description: set window group properties
help:
group [options] sets group properties for a window, such as how it behaves in a group (e.g., tabbed layout).
Options may include tab, nogroup, or others depending on Hyprland's group feature.

Examples:

    group tab → make the window join a tabbed group

    group nogroup → prevent the window from joining any group

name: suppressevent
description: ignores specific events from the window
help:
suppressevent [types...] tells Hyprland to ignore specific window events.
Supported events: fullscreen, maximize, activate, activatefocus, fullscreenoutput

Examples:

    suppressevent fullscreen maximize → ignore fullscreen and maximize requests

    suppressevent activate activatefocus → prevent the window from stealing focus

name: content
description: sets content type
help:
content [type] sets the content type of the window, helping Hyprland apply optimizations.
Available types: none, photo, video, game

Examples:

    content game → optimize for games (e.g., latency improvements)

    content video → optimize for video playback
